courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Macromolecular Crystallographic Methods
courses.description: A combined lecture/laboratory workshop for serious students of protein crystallography covering crystallization, x-ray diffraction data acquisition, and data handling. Course intended primarily for graduate students. Students are recommended to pair this course with BIOC 669 .

source.text: PHCO 667. | 2 Credits. | Prerequisite, permission of the instructor. | BIOC 667 .

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Macromolecular Crystallographic Methods II
courses.description: A combined lecture/laboratory workshop for serious students of protein crystallography or cryo-electron microscopy, addressing experimental model building, refinement, and analysis. Course intended primarily for graduate students. BIOC 667 is recommended for crystallography students. Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

source.text: PHCO 669. | 1 Credits. | Prerequisite, BIOC 666 or BIOC 675 . | BIOC 669 .

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Introduction to Molecular Pharmacology
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. A first-year pharmacology course outlining the basics of molecular pharmacology, including molecular biology, drug and receptor interactions, receptors and ion channels, regulation of second messengers, and drug metabolism. Three lecture hours a week.

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Principles of Pharmacology and Physiology
courses.description: Introduces students to the major areas of pharmacology and physiology and serves as a basis for more advanced courses. Three lecture hours a week.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, CHEM 430; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: PHCO 702. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, CHEM 430 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite. | TOXC 702 .

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Behavioral Pharmacology
courses.description: Basic principles of pharmacology and behavior analysis are considered in relation to drugs that affect the central nervous system.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, PSYC 404; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: PHCO 705. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, PSYC 404 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite. | PSYC 705 , NBIO 705 .

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Advanced Toxicology
courses.description: Cellular and physiological basis of toxicity of environmental chemicals, with emphasis on inhalation toxicology, developmental toxicology, immunotoxicology, radiation toxicology, renal toxicology, and neurotoxicology. Three lecture hours per week.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, ENVR 430; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: PHCO 707. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, ENVR 430 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite. | TOXC 707 , ENVR 707 .

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Cellular and Molecular Neurobiology: Introduction and Electrical Signaling
courses.description: Permission of the department. This course explores the experimental and theoretical function of the nervous system. Typically, the first hour is fundamental material presentation and the second hour may be a presentation led by the students. Topics covered include: cellular diversity in the CNS, gross brain anatomy, human and rodent brain imaging, neuromolecular genetics, behavioral methods, membrane potentials/resistance/capacitance, ion channel structure, electrophysiology and propagation of electrical signals in neurons. Basic undergraduate biology, chemistry, physics and intro calculus is assumed.

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Cellular and Molecular Neurobiology: Postsynaptic Mechanisms-Receptors
courses.description: Permission of the department. Consideration of membrane receptor molecules activated by neurotransmitters in the nervous system with emphasis on ligand binding behavior and molecular and functional properties of different classes of receptors. Course meets for four weeks with six lecture hours per week.

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Signal Transduction
courses.description: Seminar/discussion course on molecular aspects of the receptors, G-proteins, effector proteins, kinases, and phosphatases that mediate hormone, neurotransmitter, growth factor, and sensory signaling.

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Adhesion Receptors and Signaling in Cancer and CV Disease
courses.description: Examines the growing number of families of cell adhesion receptors and their role in biological processes including signal transduction, control of gene expression, hemostasis, cancer, neuronal development, immunobiology, and embryologic development.

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Structure and Function of Ion Channels
courses.description: Seminar/discussion course on the physiology, pharmacology, biochemistry, and molecular biology of ion channel proteins.

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Neuropharmacology of Alcohol and Substance Use
courses.description: A lecture/discussion course on the biological bases of alcohol and substance abuse.

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Gene Therapy: Medicine for the 21st Century
courses.description: A seminar/discussion course on recent advances in targeted gene delivery and gene therapy.

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Seminar in Recent Advances in Pharmacology
courses.description: Students meet as a group with faculty members to develop skills in critical reading and to summarize and discuss selected aspects of current pharmacological literature. Two hours a week. Fall and spring.

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Grant Writing
courses.description: A discussion course covering the elements of successful grant proposals and scientific ethics.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, PHCO 701; Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: PHCO 732. | 2 Credits. | Prerequisite, PHCO 701 ; Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Drug Discovery and Development
courses.description: A seminar/discussion course on the research, development, and regulatory processes involved in bringing new drugs to clinical use.

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Pain and Analgesia
courses.description: A lecture/discussion course on pain transmission and pain measurement. The neuropharmacological basis of pain modulation will be discussed.

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Discovery Biology and Pharmacogenomics
courses.description: Lecture/discussion course covering a variety of aspects of new biological and computational technologies. The course is predominantly in a lecture format with computer-based and literature assignments.

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Protein Kinases as Targets for Novel Pharmacological Inhibitors
courses.description: A seminar/discussion course to evaluate the use of small molecule inhibitors of protein kinases from a structural and signal transduction perspective.

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Target-Based Drug Discovery and Cancer Treatment
courses.description: A lecture/discussion course that emphasizes preclinical and clinical studies for the development of anti-cancer drugs that target signal transduction. Topics include: target identification and validation, drug discovery, the process of government approval for clinical trials, design of clinical trials, and new genetic-based technologies to foster drug development.

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Reprogramming of Somatic and Stem Cells and Its Applications in Pharmacology
courses.description: The objective of this new elective is to provide graduate students with an overview of stem cell biology with a unique emphasis on the applications of stem cells in pharmacology, particularly in areas of cancer and tissue regeneration.

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Contemporary Topics in Cell Signaling: Phosphorylation Control
courses.description: Required preparation, coursework in biochemistry, pharmacology and/or cell & molecular biology. Permission of the instructor. This graduate-level course is an in-depth analysis of how protein kinases and protein phosphorylation regulates key aspects of cell signaling. This class is one of the "Contemporary Topics in Cell Signaling" modules.

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Contemporary Topics in Cell Signaling: GTPases
courses.description: Required preparation, coursework in biochemistry, pharmacology, and/or cell & molecular biology. Permission of the instructor. This graduate-level course conveys principles of signal transduction controlled by GTPases and emphasizes in-depth discussion of current literature and unanswered questions. This class is one of the "Contemporary Topics in Cell Signaling" modules.

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Contemporary Topics in Cell Signaling: Cell Cycle Control
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Required preparation, coursework in biochemistry and/or cell & molecular biology. This graduate-level course conveys principles of eukaryotic cell proliferation control emphasizing in-depth discussion of current literature and unanswered questions. This class is one of the Contemporary Topics in Cell Signaling modules.

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Contemporary Topics in Cell Signaling: Signaling Networks
courses.description: Acquire the scientific vocabulary of the signaling network field. Master key concepts from mathematical characterization of signaling circuits. Develop and apply critical analysis skills.

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Topics on Stem Cells and Development
courses.description: Required preparation, coursework in genetics, cell biology, and molecular biology. Permission of the instructor. Course addresses key issues in developmental biology focused on the role of stem cells and emphasizes in-depth discussion of current literature and unanswered questions. One of the Contemporary Topics in Cell Signaling modules.

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Intercellular Signaling in Development and Disease
courses.description: This graduate-level course concentrates on up-to-date views of intercellular signal processing, with emphasis on signal transduction mechanisms as they relate to cellular/physiological responses in both normal development and disease. Signaling mechanisms that will be discussed include autocrine, paracrine, juxtacrine signaling and cell-matrix interactions.

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Introduction to Computer Vision Tools for Modern Microscopy
courses.description: This course will introduce computer vision methods for cell biology. Each topic will be motivated with an explanation of a computational challenge, followed by a discussion of available techniques to address the need and practical examples for how to apply the techniques.

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Biological Concepts
courses.description: Overview of structures and biological determinants of conditions and diseases of the oral cavity. Both growth and development and pathophysiology will be introduced in the context of three areas of oral biology: biology of extracellular matrices, host-pathogens interactions, and orofacial neurobiology.

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Practical RNA-Seq
courses.description: This course is designed to familiarize students with everything needed to run an RNA-Seq experiment. There will be minimal emphasis on theory and heavy focus on practical aspects. There are no formal prerequisites required for this course and no prior experience with UNIX or the command line interface is expected.

courses.subject: PHCO
courses.title: Proteomics Methods and Applications
courses.description: This course will familiarize graduate students with the fundamental concepts of mass spectrometry-based proteomics with emphasis on its applications (expression proteomics, post-translational modification identification, and interactomics) and practical aspects of these applications, such as experimental design, sample preparation and data interpretation. This course is intended for 2nd year students and above who currently use or plan to use proteomics in their research.
